generatedProse.concept-context: In the School of Sport, graduate capital is easy to undersell. A sport degree builds human capital in method, measurement and the understanding of performance and health. It builds social capital through placements, clubs and coaching networks, and cultural capital in how each subject argues from its own evidence. It builds identity capital as you decide what kind of sport professional you are becoming, and psychological capital through the resilience the degree itself demands. Seeing all five is what turns a transcript into a case you can make.
generatedProse.worked-example:
Two sport coaching and physical education students reach the end of the same degree with similar marks, and both are asked in interview what they have gained.

Tom talks only about modules passed and his final grade. It is accurate, but it is all human capital, and only the paper kind. The panel learns what Tom studied, not what he can offer a club or a school, who he can work with, or how he handles setbacks.

Amara gives the grade, then adds more: a coaching placement that built a network of mentors and club contacts, sessions she planned and ran that showed how the profession works, and a demanding final-year project that proved her resilience. Amara is describing human, social, cultural and psychological capital together, with a clear sense of the coach and teacher she is becoming.

Both earned the degree. Only Amara could evaluate it across the five forms, and so made the stronger case.
generatedProse.summary: Graduate capital reframes success in the School of Sport as the resources the degree builds, not marks alone. Tomlinson's framework names five forms: human, social, cultural, identity and psychological capital. You can now explain why this reframes success, distinguish the five forms, and evaluate which ones your own sport degree is building and which you are neglecting.

check.body: A sport coaching student describes the professional networks and relationships they have built during their degree. Which form of graduate capital is this?

feedback.correct: That's right. Networks and relationships are social capital.
feedback.incorrectNotFinal: Not quite. Which form names the connections you build with other people?
feedback.incorrectFinal: Networks and relationships are social capital. Human capital is skills, cultural capital is knowing the field, and psychological capital is resilience.
